text.text: The Super Nintendo Entertainment System was released in 1990 in Japan and became Nintendo's fourth-generation console. It introduced improved graphics, enhanced sound, and support for advanced cartridge features such as additional chips and battery-backed saves. The system's library included many influential games including Super Mario World, The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past, Super Metroid, Chrono Trigger, Final Fantasy VI, Donkey Kong Country, and Street Fighter II. The SNES controller introduced shoulder buttons that became a standard feature on later gamepads. The console competed directly with the Sega Genesis and remains one of Nintendo's most recognized systems.
